title: Keep every TypeScript file reachable from a structural root

facts.note: File extension .ts/.tsx; the invariant covers every eligible file in a scanned tree, including pre-existing files, not only changed ones.
Scripts in the nearest package.json declare structural roots; editing them can change reachability without any TS edit.
Emitted by bun_ts_metrics_detector after a whole-tree scan of the import graph.

fires: A .ts file (new or pre-existing) is in neither the forward nor the backward reachable set of any structural root (index/wagon/composition/main/app or a package.json script target).
A module's only connection to any structural root, in either direction, is an `import type` edge, so it has no runtime edge to the graph.
A package.json script that ran a file is removed, and that file is not otherwise reachable forwards or backwards from any remaining structural root.
doesNotFire: The file is a test file.
The scan root contains no structural root at all (it is skipped).
The file is itself the target of a script in the nearest package.json (e.g. `bun run docs/gen.ts`).
The file has no importer but itself imports, at runtime, a module that reaches a structural root (backward reachability).
The import specifier is an npm/bare package (outside the graph).

given: A TS/TSX file in a scan root that contains a structural root
when: The tree is scanned (any file, existing or changed, including package.json script edits)
then: Every TypeScript/TSX file MUST be reachable, forwards or backwards, from a structural root through runtime (non-type-only) import edges.
prefer: First decide if the file should exist at runtime: what responsibility it claims, which module would naturally import it, and whether it is obsolete, half-integrated, or types-only.
Wire required runtime behavior through the module that owns it.
Move a type into its using module when the file has no runtime values.
avoid: Dummy imports, barrel exports or other synthetic edges solely for reachability.
Side-effect imports unless the side effect is required runtime behavior.
Renaming/relocating a file merely to exploit structural-root detection.
Treating an `import type` referrer as keeping a module alive.
unless: A scan root with no structural root is skipped.
why: An unreachable file signals unclear ownership or incomplete integration, not a request to manufacture an edge; repair by removing code with no runtime responsibility or connecting it through its real owner.
evidence: The reachability finding is gone after the change.
Any new import represents a real runtime dependency (not type-only, not synthetic, not a gratuitous side-effect import).
Deleted code has no required caller or entry point.
No new architecture or dependency-flow violation was created.
The refactor introduces no new ATDD Bun violations.
Existing behavior and tests remain green.
verifier_detail: Term `structural_root`: a file the graph is walked from — a file named index, wagon, composition, main or app, or a file a script in the nearest package.json runs (e.g. `bun run docs/gen.ts`), since the repository itself declares it as an entry point.
Build the file import graph, walk it from the structural roots in both directions (forwards and backwards), and report every file in neither reachable set.
Import specifiers resolve relative or through the `@/` alias; npm/bare specifiers are outside the graph by construction.
Term `type_only_import`: an `import type` edge. Erased at compile time, so it creates no runtime edge and cannot keep a module alive — a distinction a regex cannot make and Bun's parser can.

The import graph is built with Bun's in-process TypeScript parser, which returns actual import records and omits type-only ones. Unlike the Python sibling's five-regex reader (which cannot distinguish `import type { T } from "./t"` from a value import and so counts a module whose only referrer is a type import as reachable — though it is dead), this detector reports such modules as dead. Same obligation, measured correctly — available only because the runtime is Bun; this rule is MORE ACCURATE than its Python sibling and this is the one place the port is not a transcription.
Fixture check: on a fixture where the Python detector finds one dead file, this detector finds two.
Exclusions: index.ts/index.tsx never reported; test files excluded as entrypoints; scan roots with no structural root skipped rather than reporting every file as dead.
Realized by `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (validator); core alias DEAD-CODE-REACHABILITY-TS-001; severity 2; disposition strict.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Aliases: DEAD-CODE-REACHABILITY-TS-001 — the shared core alias, also carried by the agnostic node and its python-pytest realization.

Stack-neutral obligation, NATIVE BUN detector; traversal and root vocabulary transcribed from the python-pytest sibling `coder.dead-code.reachability-typescript`, but the import graph is built by Bun's in-process TypeScript parser rather than by regex.
The Python detector reads imports with five regexes — the best a Python process can do without a TypeScript parser.

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.justification: Required by the target structure; derived only from the statement, terms (structural_root incl. package.json scripts, type_only_import) and exceptions. No phase or change-only restriction: the source states a whole-tree invariant.

additions.text: Do not treat an `import type` referrer as keeping a module alive.
additions.justification: Restates the source's type_only_import term as a coder-facing anti-pattern; no new obligation.
Makes explicit the source's definition that type-only imports create no runtime edge.
